# 12. Smalltalk interop

<!-- Generated by tools/generate-docs.lisp from docs/manual/chapters.lisp,
     docs/manual/introduction.md and the examples: do not edit by hand. -->

cog-lisp runs inside a Pharo image, and every Smalltalk object and message is
within reach: send a message with [receiver selector arg ...].

## Sending messages to Smalltalk objects

`examples/interop-send.lisp`:

```scheme
; send compiles to a real Smalltalk message send. The selector is written as in
; Smalltalk: unary, binary, or keyword.
(display (send "cog-lisp" size))                 ; unary: 8
(newline)
(display (send 3 + 4))                           ; binary: 7
(newline)
(display (send 7 between:and: 1 10))             ; keyword: #t
(newline)

; Brackets read as send, one message per pair, and read like Smalltalk.
(display ["hello" asUppercase])
(newline)
(display ["cog-lisp" reversed])
(newline)
(display [[3 @ 4] + 1])                          ; a Point
(newline)

; LISP strings and numbers are Smalltalk strings and numbers: nothing is converted.
(define greeting "Hello, Smalltalk")
(display [greeting copyReplaceAll: "Smalltalk" with: "cog-lisp"])
(newline)
(display [[2 raisedTo: 100] printStringBase: 16])    ; a big integer, in hex
(newline)

; Smalltalk globals: (smalltalk Name), or a capitalized receiver in brackets.
(define coll [OrderedCollection new])
[coll add: 3]
[coll add: 1]
[coll add: 2]
(display coll)
(newline)
(display [coll inject: 0 into: +])               ; a LISP procedure as the block
(newline)
(display (send (smalltalk Character) value: 955))
(newline)

; Dynamic sends, for selectors computed while the program runs.
(define pick (smalltalk-selector "copyFrom:to:"))
(display (smalltalk-send "interop" pick 1 5))
(newline)
(display (smalltalk-send 12 'gcd: 18))
(newline)
```

Its output:

```text
8
7
#t
HELLO
psil-goc
#<(4@5)>
Hello, cog-lisp
10000000000000000000000000
#<an OrderedCollection(3 1 2)>
6
λ
inter
6
```

## The values the two languages see differently

`examples/interop-values.lisp`:

```scheme
; Smalltalk methods often answer nil for "nothing". It reaches LISP as itself,
; prints as #<nil>, and -- like everything but #f -- counts as true.
(define table [Dictionary new])
[table at: 'one put: 1]
(define missing [table at: 'two ifAbsent: smalltalk-nil])
(display missing)
(newline)
(display (smalltalk-nil? missing))
(newline)
(display (if missing "nil is true in LISP" "nil is false"))
(newline)

; LISP symbols and Smalltalk symbols are different objects.
(define st-sym (smalltalk-symbol 'hello))
(display st-sym)
(newline)
(display (list (symbol? st-sym) (string? st-sym) (symbol? (lisp-symbol st-sym))))
(newline)
(display (eq? 'hello (lisp-symbol st-sym)))
(newline)

; Lists and Smalltalk collections convert explicitly.
(define arr (list->array '(3 1 2)))
(display arr)
(newline)
(display [arr asSortedCollection])
(newline)
(display (array->list [arr reversed]))
(newline)
(display (array->list [[1 to: 5] collect: (lambda (n) (* n n))]))
(newline)

; Any other Smalltalk object prints as #<...>, so it is never mistaken for LISP data.
(display (list (smalltalk OrderedCollection) [3 @ 4] (smalltalk-nil) 'lisp-symbol "a string"))
(newline)
(display (map smalltalk-object? (list [Set new] 42 "s" 'x car (smalltalk-nil))))
(newline)
```

Its output:

```text
#<nil>
#t
nil is true in LISP
#<#hello>
(#f #f #t)
#t
#(3 1 2)
#<a SortedCollection(1 2 3)>
(2 1 3)
(1 4 9 16 25)
(#<OrderedCollection> #<(3@4)> #<nil> lisp-symbol a string)
(#t #f #f #f #f #t)
```

## Smalltalk's collections, driven from LISP

`examples/interop-collections.lisp`:

```scheme
; An OrderedCollection, filled and queried.
(define langs [OrderedCollection new])
(for-each (lambda (s) [langs add: s]) '("Smalltalk" "Lisp" "Self" "Scheme" "Simula"))
(display [langs size])
(newline)

; LISP procedures are the blocks: select:, collect:, detect:ifNone:, inject:into:.
(display [langs select: (lambda (s) [s beginsWith: "S"])])
(newline)
(display [langs collect: (lambda (s) [s size])])
(newline)
(display [langs detect: (lambda (s) (> [s size] 6)) ifNone: (lambda () "none")])
(newline)
(display [langs inject: 0 into: (lambda (total s) (+ total [s size]))])
(newline)

; Sorting with a LISP comparison.
(display [langs asSortedCollection: (lambda (a b) (< [a size] [b size]))])
(newline)
(display [[langs collect: (lambda (s) [s asLowercase])] asSortedCollection])
(newline)

; A Dictionary used as a table, with a LISP procedure for the missing case.
(define ages [Dictionary new])
[ages at: "Smalltalk" put: 1972]
[ages at: "Lisp" put: 1958]
[ages at: "Scheme" put: 1975]
(display [ages at: "Lisp"])
(newline)
(display [ages at: "Rust" ifAbsent: (lambda () "unknown")])
(newline)
(display (array->list [[ages keys] asSortedCollection: (lambda (a b) (< [ages at: a] [ages at: b]))]))
(newline)

; Sets drop duplicates; intervals count.
(define seen [Set new])
[seen addAll: (list->array '(1 2 2 3 3 3))]
(display [seen size])
(newline)
(display (array->list [[1 to: 10 by: 3] asArray]))
(newline)
```

Its output:

```text
5
#<an OrderedCollection('Smalltalk' 'Self' 'Scheme' 'Simula')>
#<an OrderedCollection(9 4 4 6 6)>
Smalltalk
29
#<a SortedCollection('Lisp' 'Self' 'Scheme' 'Simula' 'Smalltalk')>
#<a SortedCollection('lisp' 'scheme' 'self' 'simula' 'smalltalk')>
1958
unknown
(Lisp Smalltalk Scheme)
3
(1 4 7 10)
```

## Word frequencies with Smalltalk streams and a Bag

A small, practical program: LISP for the logic, Smalltalk's library for the parts.

`examples/interop-streams.lisp`:

```scheme
(define text "the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog the fox runs and the dog sleeps")

; Split the text into words with a ReadStream.
(define (words-of s)
  (let ((in [ReadStream on: s])
        (words [OrderedCollection new]))
    (let loop ()
      (when (not [in atEnd])
        (let ((w [in upTo: #\space]))
          (when (not [w isEmpty]) [words add: w]))
        (loop)))
    words))

; Count them with a Bag, then sort by count (and by word, for ties).
(define (frequencies words)
  (let ((bag [Bag new]))
    [bag addAll: words]
    [[[bag asSet] asArray] asSortedCollection:
       (lambda (a b)
         (let ((ca [bag occurrencesOf: a])
               (cb [bag occurrencesOf: b]))
           (or (> ca cb) (and (= ca cb) (<= [a compare: b] 2)))))]))

(define words (words-of text))
(display [words size])
(display " words, ")
(display [[words asSet] size])
(display " different")
(newline)

; The top four, written to a Smalltalk WriteStream and displayed.
(define out [WriteStream on: [String new]])
(define (report word count)
  [out nextPutAll: word]
  [out nextPutAll: ": "]
  [out print: count]
  [out nextPut: #\newline])
(define bag [Bag new])
[bag addAll: words]
(for-each (lambda (w) (report w [bag occurrencesOf: w]))
          (array->list [[(frequencies words) asArray] first: 4]))
(display [out contents])
```

Its output:

```text
16 words, 11 different
the: 4
dog: 2
fox: 2
and: 1
```

## Smalltalk calling LISP

`examples/interop-callbacks.lisp`:

```scheme
; A LISP procedure works wherever Smalltalk expects a block. This one ends in a
; tail call (to its helper); it still answers a plain value to Smalltalk.
(define (classify n) (describe-parity n))
(define (describe-parity n) (if (= (modulo n 2) 0) 'even 'odd))
(display (array->list [[1 to: 4] collect: classify]))
(newline)

; A loop written as LISP tail calls, called by Smalltalk for each element.
(define (count-down n acc) (if (= n 0) acc (count-down (- n 1) (+ acc 1))))
(display (array->list [[100000 to: 100002] collect: (lambda (n) (count-down n 0))]))
(newline)

; Smalltalk errors can be caught with a LISP handler: on:do: with LISP
; procedures as both the protected block and the handler.
(display [(lambda () (/ 1 0)) on: (smalltalk ZeroDivide) do: (lambda (e) "caught a division by zero")])
(newline)
(display [(lambda () [3 frobnicate]) on: (smalltalk MessageNotUnderstood)
                                      do: (lambda (e) [[e message] selector])])
(newline)

; ensure: runs its LISP block however the protected one ends.
(define log '())
[(lambda () (set! log (cons 'body log))) ensure: (lambda () (set! log (cons 'cleanup log)))]
(display (reverse log))
(newline)

; procedure->block makes a real BlockClosure, for code that needs one.
(define blk (procedure->block (lambda (a b) (* a b))))
(display (list [blk class] [blk numArgs] [blk value: 6 value: 7]))
(newline)

; Smalltalk can evaluate and call LISP through the CogLisp class.
(define (square x) (* x x))
(display [CogLisp call: "square" with: 12])
(newline)
(display [CogLisp eval: "(map square '(1 2 3))"])
(newline)
(display [[CogLisp at: "square"] value: 9])
(newline)
```

Its output:

```text
(odd even odd even)
(100000 100001 100002)
caught a division by zero
#<#frobnicate>
(body cleanup)
(#<FullBlockClosure> 2 42)
144
(1 4 9)
81
```
